title: An image can now become a video
summary:
New models expanded what you can make, while usage, keys, and image requests became easier to understand and harder to trip over.

Wan 2.6 joined the lineup as `wan`, turning an input image into a 720P video lasting 2–15 seconds, with auto-dubbed audio on by default. The model list also gained `gemini-legacy` for Gemini 2.5 Pro and `klein-large` for FLUX.2 Klein 9B image generation and editing. Klein 9B carries a non-commercial license.

Flux gained room for up to 1024×1024 total pixels, while z-image now rejects oversized requests instead of silently shrinking them and upscales outputs above its native generation limit. Klein editing request formats were aligned across variants, and image requests without an explicit model use the default again.

Account profiles gained a timestamp for the next daily Pollen reset. Enter added daily request and Pollen graphs with time-range, API-key, and model filters; a daily usage endpoint provides grouped JSON or CSV, and detailed exports now allow up to 50,000 records. Usage reporting also separates audio seconds from video usage.

The new `GET /api/account/key` endpoint checks validity, expiry, permissions, remaining Pollen budget, and rate-limit status without generating anything. Higher verification capacity helps concurrent requests avoid erroneous 401s; rate limiting now returns 429, while insufficient Pollen or an exhausted key budget returns 402 rather than an access-denied 403. BYOD authorization also accepts longer redirect hostnames.
